why: After Daniel's first 7 edits (S1-Mini-Cleanup-Finetune notes/annotation-patterns.md): what his edits do and stock S1-mini doesn't.

kind_desc.ai_prompt: a prompt being dictated to an AI assistant
kind_desc.note: a note to himself being dictated

email: to his wife Hannah about a household matter
to a landlord about a repair
to a colleague about a project
to a client after a first meeting
to a doctor's office to reschedule
to a school about a child's schedule
to a supplier about an order
to a new client after a call
message: a message to a group chat
a reply to a colleague on Slack
a message to a delivery driver
a message to the building committee (vaad bayit)
a reply to a friend's invitation
a text to Hannah with three quick things
calendar: a reminder to pay a bill
two related appointments in one go
a reminder with a deadline that changes mid-sentence
a call with someone whose name he spells out
ai_prompt: a prompt to Claude Code about a bug in a web app
a prompt asking an AI to research a purchase
a prompt to an agent to reorganise files on a server
a prompt to draft a blog post outline
a prompt asking for a shell script
a prompt asking an AI to compare two speech models
a prompt to an agent to set up a Home Assistant automation
a follow-up correcting what an AI just did
note: a to-do brain dump for the day
notes on a meeting just finished
a journal entry about the week
a plan for a home office upgrade
thoughts on training a speech model

features: a greeting at the start and a spoken sign-off at the end
an aside that clarifies something in passing ("the one for the Rehavia apartment", "just so it doesn't time out")
a self-correction that changes a date, time or amount twice before settling
a name or word spelled out letter by letter for the transcriber
several separate requests or items run together in one sentence
a long run-on sentence joined with "and" and "so"
an immediate repeated word or phrase ("the, the")
a false start that is restarted
a word aside to someone else in the room ("one sec, Noa, put that down")
"where was I" or a similar recovery phrase
a thank-you said in passing in the middle
